name: Geography of Indian - Improved Historical Chronology
description: Comprehensive timeline of Harappan, Early Indian Cultures, and subsequent empires showing sequential and parallel historical developments.

events.name: Paleolithic
events.notesMarkdown: Era of earliest human use of large stone tools.

events.name: Mesolithic
events.notesMarkdown: Transition period featuring the use of smaller stone tools.

events.name: Neolithic
events.notesMarkdown: Polished stone tools era. In South India, this ran parallel to the Harappan civilization in the North, and supplied gold to them.

events.name: Neolithic culture of Mehrgarh
events.notesMarkdown: Earliest agricultural settlements in the subcontinent where Neolithic humans lived before eventually migrating toward the Indus River to form the early Harappan culture.

events.name: Chalcolithic
events.notesMarkdown: Transition period using both stone and copper tools.

events.name: Early Harappan Phase
events.notesMarkdown: A rural, Chalcolithic phase characterized by regional diversity as populations settled along the Indus.

resources.label: Harappan - Indus Valley Civilization Malayalam Explanation

events.name: Bronze Age
events.notesMarkdown: Marked by the mixture of copper and tin for sharper tools. This aligns precisely with the Mature Harappan unification.

events.name: Mature Harappan Phase
events.notesMarkdown: An urban, Bronze Age phase marked by unified town planning, writing, and active trade with Mesopotamia. Parallel Incident: This culture was younger than Mesopotamia, but co-existed with it.

events.name: Ganeshwar-Jodhpura Culture
events.notesMarkdown: Parallel Incident: A rural Chalcolithic culture using copper tools that existed completely contemporaneously with the urban Mature Harappan civilization, located in Rajasthan.

events.name: Late Harappan Phase
events.notesMarkdown: Decline of urban uniformity. Harappans abandoned writing and Bronze, migrating to new areas like Swat, Jhukar, Rangpur, and Siswal.

events.name: Banas Culture (Rajasthan)
events.notesMarkdown: A post-Harappan rural Chalcolithic culture.

events.name: Kayatha Culture (Madhya Pradesh)
events.notesMarkdown: A rural Chalcolithic culture.

events.name: Savalda Culture (Tapi Valley)
events.notesMarkdown: A rural Chalcolithic culture located in the Tapi Valley.

events.name: Prabhas Culture (Saurashtra Coast)
events.notesMarkdown: A rural Chalcolithic culture.

events.name: Malwa Culture (West Madhya Pradesh)
events.notesMarkdown: A rural Chalcolithic culture.

events.name: Jorwe Culture (Maharashtra)
events.notesMarkdown: A post-Harappan Chalcolithic culture found in Maharashtra.

events.name: Rigvedic (Early Vedic) Period
events.notesMarkdown: Key Event: Arrival of Aryans marking a Chalcolithic phase in Northern India. Pastoral tribe life.

events.name: Iron Age
events.notesMarkdown: Began around 1000 BC. Parallel Incident: This covers the Later Vedic period (Painted Grey Ware) in North India and simultaneously the Megalithic period in South India.

events.name: Later Vedic Period (Painted Grey Ware)
events.notesMarkdown: Key Factor: Introduction of iron in North India, shift to settled life.

events.name: Megalithic Culture (South India)
events.notesMarkdown: Parallel Incident: The use of iron and large stones in South India ran contemporaneously with the Later Vedic period in North India.

events.name: Post-Vedic / Mahajanapada Period
events.notesMarkdown: Period of political fragmentation. 16 prominent states (Mahajanapadas) formed, including monarchies like Magadha and republics like Malla.

events.name: Persian Invasion
events.notesMarkdown: Parallel Incident: Occurred while India was fragmented into 16 Mahajanapadas.

events.name: Mauryan Empire
events.notesMarkdown: First major political unification and highly centralized power in North India. Parallel Incident: Diplomatic relations established with Greek ambassador Megasthenes during Chandragupta's reign.

events.name: Early South Indian Empires (Chera, Chola, Pandya)
events.notesMarkdown: Key Factor: Maintained extraordinary continuity for approx 1600 years. Parallel Incident: Ran concurrent to the Mauryan, Post-Mauryan, Gupta, and Early Medieval empires of the North due to geographic isolation.

events.name: Post-Mauryan Period (Political Fragmentation)
events.notesMarkdown: Empire fragmented into regional powers like Shungas, Kanvas, and Satavahanas. Khayber Pass left unprotected, inviting multiple central Asian invasions.

events.name: Indo-Greeks & Central Asian Invasions
events.notesMarkdown: Sequential Invasions via Khyber pass: Indo-Greeks (2nd to 1st C BC), followed by Shakas (1st C BC to 4th C AD), Parthians, and Kushanas.

events.name: Gupta Period
events.notesMarkdown: Brought a new wave of political unification. Parallel Incident: Co-existed with regional kingdoms like Vakatakas in Central India and Pallavas/Kadambas in the South.

events.name: Pallava Dynasty
events.notesMarkdown: Key Factor: Temporarily replaced the Cholas in South India. They were contemporary with the Guptas, Harsha, and early Chalukyas.

events.name: Era of Harshavardhana & Chalukyas
events.notesMarkdown: Briefly unified North India post-Gupta decline. Parallel Incident: Fought extensively with his Southern contemporary, Pulakeshin of the Chalukyas.

events.name: Tripartite Struggle (Rajput Era)
events.notesMarkdown: Intense triangular conflict over Kannauj involving Gurjara-Pratiharas, Rashtrakutas, and Palas.

events.name: Arab Invasion of Sindh
events.notesMarkdown: Led by Muhammad bin Qasim. Parallel Incident: Faced heavy resistance from the contemporary Gurjara-Pratihara Rajputs, stopping their spread.

events.name: Mahmud of Ghazni Invasions
events.notesMarkdown: Key Factor: Exploited the political fragmentation of the Late Rajput era. Avoided dominant powers like Chandellas and Paramaras to plunder weaker territories.

events.name: Delhi Sultanate
events.notesMarkdown: Formed following Ghori's victory at Tarain. Parallel Incident: Their foreign policy constantly adapted to the massive Mongol threat (isolation under Iltutmish, defense under Balban, offense under Alauddin Khilji).

events.name: Bahmani & Vijayanagara Empires
events.notesMarkdown: Emerged to fill the vacuum in South India after the Delhi Sultanate lost control. Vijayanagara collapsed at the Battle of Talikota in 1565.

events.name: Arrival of the Portuguese
events.notesMarkdown: Vasco da Gama arrived 1498. Parallel Incident: Captured Goa from Bijapur in 1510, and acquired Diu from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in the 1530s, exactly contemporary with early Mughal Emperor Humayun.
